notes: Both coders found the same two university-layer documents (provost letter 2023, Eberly sample syllabus statements) and both set stance restrict and delegates. Main disagreements: (1) modality for the quoted sample statements, where the source verb decides: "you should complete" and "Please refrain" are should/should-not, "I encourage" is should not may, "I expect ... their own" is must, and "Deviations ... will be considered violations" is must-not; (2) unit_stance, where neutral vs prohibit/require was resolved by whether the sentence takes a position on AI use itself (uncited-use and verify-output duties are neutral; the bibliography bar is prohibit); (3) phase and actor for default rules and sample statements (default fallback rules are general; sentences addressed to students about their assignment work are student/during-work; the rationale "Learning how to use AI is an emerging skill" is all/general/neutral); (4) policy_type P25 vs P26 for the exact prompt and full response in an Appendix (P25) and P04 vs P05 for the "range of options" sentence (P04). Only-A units (4: ask-me sentence, code generation models inaccurate, smaller-sample citation, Example 5 deviations) were all real and kept. Only-B unit (1: "may not attempt to pass off any work generated by an AI program as your own") was real and kept. B left every policy null; A normalized many, and the final file keeps A's wording after checking each against the source (the Example 4 non-text item gained its condition "when expressly permitted in the assignment prompt", the Example 5 note and Example 6 examples were reworded to match the source).
